issue.title: Mechanical inline-vs-monitor routing in sase tool run: per-tool duration classes plus SASE_PROVIDER_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-177.4 (epic sase-177, Muse single-turn normalization; plan
plan:202609/muse_single_turn_normalization.md, "Follow-ups" item 1). The user deferred
this out of the epic during planning and asked for a post-landing `large` task.

Today routing a command to a monitor versus inline is a prompt rule only (the Muse
single-turn directive in src/sase/llm_provider/muse.py, /sase_monitor "Decide Before You
Start", and lint_and_test.md's list of known-long commands). Make it mechanical:

- Declare a duration class per tool catalog entry (`short`, `long`, `unbounded`).
- Provider adapters export `SASE_PROVIDER_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS` (600 for Muse with
  muse_synchronous_shell on; see `_MUSE_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS`).
- `sase tool run` refuses, before starting, a `long`/`unbounded` tool whose class floor
  exceeds the caller's ceiling, and prints the exact prepared-completion or `--next`
  monitor command to use instead (follows decisions:guarded-recipes).
- Use the ToolRun duration corpus for calibration, not as the gate.
- Crosses the sase-core boundary: Rust wire/API, binding, tests, and the
  sase-core-revision.txt pin.
